agents.notes: Both concept ViewSets set http_method_names=["head","get","put"] (chiron/api_v2/viewsets/concept.py:52, chiron/api/viewsets/concept.py:53), so ONLY GET/HEAD/PUT are dispatched. Standard actions enabled: list(GET), retrieve(GET), update(PUT). create/partial_update/destroy are NOT enabled. IMPORTANT: cohort_def_callback and cohort_def_callback_streaming are declared @action(methods=["GET","POST"]) but a POST is rejected 405 because 'post' is absent from http_method_names — effectively GET-only. ConceptViewSet.update()/retrieve() do not persist anything; PUT just lets the client pass long params (cohort_def etc.) in the body instead of the query string. list() is paginated (PageNumberPagination, page_size 100, max 1000, ?page & ?page_size); retrieve/update return a bare object. concept_categories list/retrieve/concept_search return custom dicts and are NOT paginated. Two ConceptSerializer definitions exist and differ: v2 (chiron/api_v2/serializers/concept.py:25) includes a 'pk' field; v1 (chiron/api/serializers.py:83) is identical minus 'pk'. ConceptCategoryViewSetV2 extends the v1 ConceptCategoryViewSet and, via inherited _fetch_concepts_and_categories plus its own concept_search, serializes concepts with the v1 ConceptSerializer (no pk) even though it lives on the v2 surface — a mild inconsistency. CategorySerializer is shared (v1 module) by both surfaces. Response 'statistics'/'cohort_def_options'/'table_def_options'/'callback_data' payloads are dynamic and produced by per-concept processors (get_form_options/get_statistics/form_callback) — shapes vary by concept handler and are not statically declarable; error branches return {'error': <reason>}. v1 vs v2 helper divergence: v2 helpers read cohort_def/table_def from query_params (falling back to active snapshot) and are dataset-scoped via collection__dataset__unique_id=dataset_string / request.dataset; v1 _get_concept_statistics and _get_cohort_def_options always use the active snapshot (ignore a cohort_def param) and query Concept.objects globally (Concept.objects.all(), no dataset filter). v2 routes carry (?P<dataset_string>.+) captured from the URL; v1 routes are flat and resolve the dataset via DatasetSelector/request.dataset. Retrieve lookup for concepts is permanent_id (lookup_field); for concept_categories it is the default pk (int). Streaming endpoints emit JSON segments joined by the literal separator '**split**' (make_json_encodable applied)."
open_questions: DatasetUrlPermission (v2) and DatasetSelector (v1) presumably set request.dataset/request.chironuser; not read here — exact resolution of dataset_string -> Dataset and the 403/404 behavior for a missing/unauthorized dataset was not verified.

get_stattool / processor.get_form_options / get_statistics / form_callback define the concrete shapes of statistics, cohort_def_options, table_def_options and callback_data; these were not opened, so those sub-payloads remain 'dynamic object'.
get_concept_type returns processor.concept_type; the full set of possible string values (beyond 'unknown') was not enumerated.

The regex prefix (?P<dataset_string>.+) is greedy and registered before collections/reports/etc.; whether ordering causes any route-matching ambiguity across v2 resources was not analyzed (out of scope but worth confirming).

agents.notes:
SCOPE: collections (v1 + v2) and datasets (v2 only). No v1 'datasets' resource exists — v1 selects dataset via session (DatasetSelector). Mount prefixes: /api/ (chiron/urls.py:101) and /api/v2/ (chiron/urls.py:102).

COLLECTIONS are READ-ONLY on both surfaces. v1 CollectionViewSet extends DRF ReadOnlyModelViewSet, so only list + retrieve exist (no create/update/partial_update/destroy). v2 CollectionViewSetV2 subclasses the v1 viewset, inheriting serializer_class (CollectionSerializer), lookup_field='permanent_id', retrieve(), and the criteria-set helper methods; it overrides get_queryset (scopes to chironuser.dataset from URL) and sets pagination_class=None.

PAGINATION: v1 collections list has NO pagination_class set, so it uses the project DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS. In the repo's shipped settings (test_project/test_settings.py:113) that is PageNumberPagination with PAGE_SIZE=10 -> count/next/previous/results wrapper. If a deploying project sets DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS=None the v1 list would return a bare array. v2 collections list is explicitly non-paginated (bare array). v2 dataset list/retrieve are plain viewsets.ViewSet actions, never paginated.

RENDERERS: v1 CollectionViewSet declares renderer_classes = [JSONRenderer, CollectionTemplateRenderer (text/plain), BrowsableAPIRenderer (text/html)] (chiron/api/viewsets/collection.py:24-30). So response format varies by Accept header; JSON field shapes documented above apply to application/json. v2 uses default JSON.

CollectionSerializer (chiron/api/serializers.py:142) is a ModelSerializer exposing ONLY: permanent_id, name, get_name_plural, is_root_collection, has_event. get_name_plural and is_root_collection are model callables/properties rendered read-only; has_event is a SerializerMethodField. No write fields (read-only endpoint).

DATASET v2 list response only includes 7 fields per dataset (id, name, description, siteTitle, unique_id, selectable, contactEmail) even though DatasetSerializer declares more — the viewset builds each dict manually with just those keys (datasets.py:34-42), and the extra serializer fields are required=False so absent. Retrieve populates the fuller set (id, name, unique_id, description, lastImport, subjectCount, accessLevelLabel, accessLevel, canViewWorkspace, canViewSubjectDetails, logoUrl, chironUserId, extraHeaderLinks). Types on the serializer are all declared as CharField/IntegerField/BooleanField/EmailField/JSONField (auth.py:11-27); subjectCount/lastImport are CharField even though semantically a count/date (formatted strings). accessLevel is the raw enum value (phi/deid/agg) while accessLevelLabel is the human-readable display.

The three requested query params (include_criteria_set_options, include_criteria_set_event_options, criteria_set_entry_id) apply to the collections RETRIEVE action on BOTH v1 and v2 (identical code, inherited). They pull from the active cohort def via qdef.get_active_cohort_def(request). When neither flag is set, the plain CollectionSerializer object is returned. When set, extra keys criteria_set_options / criteria_set_event_options / criteria_set_entry_id are merged onto the serialized dict. criteria_set_entry_id is REQUIRED when either flag is truthy (raises ValueError -> 500 otherwise).

criteria_set_options / criteria_set_event_options are hand-built dicts (not serializers). Full sub-structure of event_options entries varies by EventOption subclass (date_range, relative_to_today, relative_to_other_event, no_restriction, age_in_days variants); the abstract base guarantees option_id, label, django_template, allowed (chiron/query_definition/event_options/_abstract.py:51). selected_event_option is the unique_name string of the active option.

Present in v1 (collection.py:47-64) and v2 (collection.py:36-42). Flagged as behavior, not a documented feature.
open_questions: The ?collection= list filter references a non-existent Collection.collection field (see notes) — unclear whether this is dead code or relies on a dynamic relation I did not find; runtime behavior likely errors.

Exact production DRF pagination for v1 collections depends on the deploying project's REST_FRAMEWORK setting; only the repo's test/performance project settings were available (PageNumberPagination, PAGE_SIZE=10). No canonical prod settings module found in-repo.

Full field set of each event_options entry depends on ~9 EventOption subclasses (date_range, year_range, interval_*, relative_to_today, relative_to_other_event, age_in_days_range, no_restriction) whose get_option_data overrides were not individually opened; only the abstract base fields (option_id, label, django_template, allowed) are guaranteed.

agents.notes:
AUTH & PERMISSION MODEL (scope: auth/permissions/middleware + non-API server-rendered views).

== Request authentication ==
Authentication is standard Django. There is NO custom authentication backend in the chiron app; the demo project (test_project/project/settings.py) uses default AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS (ModelBackend) with session-based auth, django.contrib.auth.urls mounted at /accounts/ (login/logout/password reset) and admin at /admin/. LOGIN_URL is not set, so Django's default '/accounts/login/' applies. DRF has no REST_FRAMEWORK block in settings, so v1/v2 API viewsets rely on DRF defaults (SessionAuthentication + BasicAuthentication) and each viewset declares its own permission_classes (typically [IsAuthenticated, DatasetUrlPermission(, CanViewWorkspacePermission)]; the auth viewset uses AllowAny, datasets viewset uses [IsAuthenticated]).

== Two-layer identity: Django User -> ChironUser ==
Every access decision hinges on resolving a ChironUser for the (Django user, Dataset) pair. authorization.py:get_request_dataset resolves the active dataset from session['dataset_id'] (or auto-selects the single dataset if only one exists). get_request_chironuser then finds ChironUser(user, dataset); if none exists AND dataset.autocreate_chiron_user is True it creates one using the dataset's auto_* defaults (auto_access_level, auto_can_view_workspace, auto_can_view_subject_details) and attaches all DefaultPermissionGroup groups. If no ChironUser can be found/created it returns None -> access denied.

== Dataset-level enforcement (differs v1 vs v2) ==
- Server views: @dataset_selector decorator (authorization.py:76) resolves dataset from SESSION; on failure redirects to chiron:select_dataset. Sets request.dataset + request.chironuser.
- v1 API: DatasetSelector permission (api/permissions.py:8) — same session-based resolution; raises BadRequest if multiple datasets and none in session, PermissionDenied if no chironuser.
- v2 API: DatasetUrlPermission (api_v2/permissions.py:8) resolves dataset from the URL kwarg <dataset_string> via get_object_or_404(Dataset, unique_id=...) (404 if unknown), then get_request_chironuser; PermissionDenied if no chironuser. This is why the React UI (v2) is dataset-scoped by URL, not session. api_v2/authorization.py provides helpers set_chironuser_dataset() and url_dataset_check() (raise PermissionDenied if URL dataset_string missing or mismatched).
All three set request.dataset and request.chironuser as the side effect that downstream permissions depend on.

== Feature/level permissions (layered AFTER dataset resolution) ==
- can_view_workspace (authorization.py:133) / CanViewWorkspacePermission (api_v2/permissions.py:30): gate query/results/workspace features via ChironUser.can_view_workspace. Server-side uses request_passes_test(can_view_workspace) which, on failure, ALWAYS redirects to chiron:home (the login_url arg is ignored — see authorization.py:105).
- can_view_subject_details (authorization.py:145): requires can_view_subject_details AND access_level != AGG.
- SubjectLevelAccess (api/permissions.py:64): allows only access_level in {PHI, DEID}; denies AGG (aggregate-only). Raises AttributeError if request.chironuser wasn't set first.
- AnalysisViewOn (api/permissions.py:55): gates analysis view on the CHIRON_SHOW_ANALYSIS_VIEW setting.
- user_is_staff (authorization.py:13): all /backend/* views wrap @user_passes_test(user_is_staff) so they are staff-only. Exception: stop_viewing_as_user is intentionally NOT staff-gated (the impersonated user must be able to exit).

== Object-level permissions ==
UserCreatedContentPermission (api/permissions.py:32): read (SAFE_METHODS) allowed if obj.public OR shared-with-user OR obj.creator.user==user; write/delete only for the owner (obj.creator.user==user). The report server view (views.py:135) enforces the analogous rule manually via ChironUser.get_viewable_reports() and raises PermissionDenied otherwise.

== View-as-other-user (impersonation) flow ==
Middleware chiron/middleware/view_as_other_user.py:ViewAsOtherUser subclasses Django RemoteUserMiddleware but OVERRIDES process_request entirely, so it does NOT do REMOTE_USER header auth despite the base class. On every request it sets request.view_as_other_user_middleware_installed=True; if session['override_user_id'] is set and resolves to a User, it replaces request.user with that user and sets request.viewing_as_other_user=<username> (used by templates/UI banner). Flow: (1) staff posts override_user_id to /backend/user_report (views_backend.py:206) which writes session['override_user_id'] and redirects to workspace; (2) middleware then swaps request.user on subsequent requests; (3) /backend/stop_viewing_as_user (views_backend.py:196) sets session['override_user_id']=None to end impersonation. Middleware must run after SessionMiddleware and AuthenticationMiddleware (it is last in the demo MIDDLEWARE list).

== URL surface (chiron/urls.py, included at project root '') ==
Non-API server views live at /, /select_dataset, /workspace, /reports, /report/<id>, /backend/* (staff), and /ajax/* (AJAX JSON). v1 API at /api/ and v2 API at /api/v2/<dataset_string>/... are included but OUT OF SCOPE for this report (covered by other agents). Note: URL name 'ajax_view_mode_widget' maps to path /ajax/get_view_mode_selector. Several urls are commented out/disabled: single_subject*, query_troubleshooting sub-views (results_table/cohort_count/analysis_output), ajax_get_td_entry_form. data_dictionary view is present but flagged BROKEN and hidden in the UI.

Response types: /backend/* and page views return server-rendered HTML (render()); /ajax/* return JsonResponse (mostly {html, data_view_mode} or {html}); stop_viewing_as_user, select_dataset POST, and user_report POST return 302 redirects. Pagination on list-ish backend views uses Django core Paginator (etl_logs=10/page, subject-matching views=100/page), NOT DRF pagination.
open_questions: report view (views.py:135) has no @dataset_selector and, if get_request_chironuser returns None (user lacks access and dataset isn't autocreate), request.chironuser is never set — the subsequent `oContent not in request.chironuser.get_viewable_reports()` would raise AttributeError rather than a clean 403. Confirm intended behavior.

user_report POST (views_backend.py:217) does int(request.POST.get('override_user_id', None)); if the field is absent this raises TypeError(int(None)). Likely relies on the form always submitting the field. Confirm.

select_dataset POST stores any submitted dataset_id in session without verifying the user has (or can autocreate) a ChironUser for it; the access gate is deferred to the next dataset_selector call. Confirm this is intentional (defense-in-depth relies on dataset_selector).

ViewAsOtherUser subclasses RemoteUserMiddleware but fully overrides process_request — the RemoteUserMiddleware base is effectively unused. Confirm no reliance on REMOTE_USER header auth anywhere in production settings (only test_project settings were available in-repo).
No REST_FRAMEWORK settings block found in test_project; production/deployment settings (DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES, pagination, throttling) may differ and were not available in this repo.

agents.notes:
Routing: v1 mounted at 'api/' (chiron/urls.py:101), v2 at 'api/v2/' (chiron/urls.py:102). v2 routes are dataset-scoped: r'(?P<dataset_string>.+)/reports' and '.../report_tools' (chiron/api_v2/urls.py:9,28). Trailing slash is present on all DRF-router URLs.

Report viewsets: ReportViewSet (v1) and ReportViewSetV2 (v2) are DRF ModelViewSets => all six standard actions (list/retrieve/create/update/partial_update/destroy) are enabled, plus @action customs. ReportViewSetV2 subclasses nothing special but adds get_report and viewable_reports which do NOT exist in v1. Both share serializers.UserCreatedContentSerializer and identical get_queryset logic (starts from chironuser.get_viewable_reports(): type=table AND (creator OR shared OR public), distinct).

ReportTools viewsets: ReportToolsViewSet (v1) is a plain DRF ViewSet (NOT ModelViewSet) => only the explicitly-defined list/retrieve plus @actions exist; there is no create/update/destroy. ReportToolsViewSetV2 subclasses the v1 class, overriding list/retrieve (to rewrite URLs into the /api/v2/<dataset>/ namespace) and re-declaring share/load_as_active/export_csv/export_json/preview (the v2 overrides scope UserCreatedContent lookups to request.dataset; v1 does not). Note report_tools/share takes a RAW JSON array as the request body (json.loads(request.body)), not a named field.

Pagination: LargeResultsSetPagination (PageNumberPagination) wraps list responses in {count,next,previous,results}; page_size default 1000, page_size_query_param 'page_size', max_page_size 10000 (chiron/api/utils/pagination.py:6).

Serializer write behavior: UserCreatedContentSerializer.validate() (serializers.py:216) always forces creator_id and dataset_id from request context, normalizes definition.cohort_def via Cohort(), and requires data['type'] to be cohort or table. creator and created are read_only. share_with, creator_name, project_name, starred, sharing_description are all read-only (method/nested) fields. sharing_description returns 'public' | 'private' | '{n} users'.

Renderers: Report viewsets support JSON, a text/plain ReportsTemplateRenderer, and BrowsableAPI; report_tools use ReportToolsTemplateRenderer for text/plain. export_csv returns text/csv (not DRF Response). export_json/preview 'output_type' (html/json/csv) is passed through to chiron.api.utils.export helpers (generate_cohort_json / get_paginated_preview) whose exact payload shapes live in chiron/api/utils/export.py (out of scope here)."
open_questions: export_json / export_csv exact payload shapes come from chiron/api/utils/export.py (generate_cohort_csv, generate_cohort_json) and were not read in this task scope; preview field types are taken from the viewset docstring plus get_paginated_preview (export.py) — types are documented-but-not-declared and should be confirmed against export.py.

get_report response (extended_cohort_def, cohort_description, extended_table_def) structures come from chiron.query_definition (qdef.Cohort/Table/describe_cohort_def); their internal field shapes were not expanded here.

serializer.validate() references data['type'] unconditionally (serializers.py:242), so a PATCH/partial_update that omits 'type' appears to KeyError before reaching the choice check — flagged as inferred behavior, not verified at runtime.

v1 flag and v1 share look up UserCreatedContent WITHOUT dataset scoping (objects.get / get_object_or_404(UserCreatedContent)), whereas v2 scopes to request.dataset; whether v1 relies on separate permission classes to prevent cross-dataset access was not fully traced (permission classes DatasetSelector/UserCreatedContentPermission not read in full).

agents.notes:
SCOPE: cohort_def + query_tools, both v1 (/api/) and v2 (/api/v2/{dataset_string}/). URL prefixes confirmed in chiron/urls.py:101-102. Routers: chiron/api/urls.py:14,17 and chiron/api_v2/urls.py:10-12,24-26 (DRF DefaultRouter). v2 dataset_string is a greedy regex (?P<dataset_string>.+).

Both viewsets are plain rest_framework.viewsets.ViewSet (NOT ModelViewSet), so ONLY the explicitly-defined actions exist. cohort_def defines list/retrieve/create ONLY -> no update/partial_update/destroy (router emits no PUT/PATCH/DELETE). query_tools defines list + 4 custom @action methods (count, export_csv, preview_metadata, preview), each detail=False methods=[GET,POST]. No standard CRUD actions on query_tools.

V2 classes (CohortDefViewSetV2, QueryToolsViewSetV2) subclass the v1 classes and change only permission_classes (DatasetUrlPermission instead of DatasetSelector) plus CohortDefViewSetV2.get_queryset (which filters CohortDefSnapshot by chironuser but is NOT actually used by list/retrieve/create — those methods query snapshots directly). Behavior/response shapes are otherwise identical between v1 and v2.

No DRF pagination anywhere in scope: cohort_def returns bare dicts; query_tools.preview uses a custom chiron.paginator.ReportPaginator (paginator sub-object), never the DRF count/next/previous/results wrapper.

Auth: both viewsets set authentication_classes=[CsrfExemptSessionAuthentication] (session auth, CSRF-exempt). All endpoints require IsAuthenticated. renderer_classes support application/json, text/plain (custom template renderers CohortDefTemplateRenderer / QueryToolsTemplateRenderer), and text/html (BrowsableAPIRenderer); list/retrieve for cohort_def and preview_metadata pass template_name for the HTML renderer.

IMPORTANT BEHAVIORAL QUIRKS: (1) query_tools count/export_csv/preview_metadata/preview DOCUMENT cohort_def and table_def params, but _get_cohort_def/_get_table_def (query_tools.py:200-210) IGNORE request params entirely and always use the active CohortDefSnapshot/TableDefSnapshot. So those body/query params are effectively no-ops in the current code. (2) query_tools list builds URLs via reverse('chiron:api:query_tools-list') even in v2, so the v2 discovery response returns v1 (/api/) URLs, not dataset-scoped v2 URLs. (3) cohort_def.create parses the body with json.loads(request.body) rather than request.data/a serializer. (4) cohort_def 'list' returns the single active cohort def object, not a collection.

The cohort_def and query_tools viewsets use NO serializer classes — responses are hand-built dicts from qdef.Cohort/Table, export_utils, and paginator.json(). The only cohort-related serializer in chiron/api/serializers.py is UserCreatedContentSerializer (reports resource), whose validate() normalizes definition.cohort_def through Cohort(); documented as a model here for completeness.

Types marked array[string]/object/etc. are inferred from Python construction (lists, dict payloads, str()/int() casts) since there is no serializer schema. cohort_def 'count' is returned as a STRING (str(count)), not an int.

Models: The task referenced 'CohortDefinition / CriteriaSet models in chiron/models/data_definition_models.py' but NO such models exist there (that file holds Dataset/Collection/Concept/Category/PermissionGroup/Source etc.). The actual cohort persistence is CohortDefSnapshot (chiron/models/user_models.py). 'CriteriaSet' is a JSON sub-structure, documented here as the pseudo-models CohortDefCriteriaSet / CohortDefEntry / ExtendedCriteriaSet / ExtendedCdEntry with source refs to query_definition.

The task also asked to cover a 'cohort_def_callback' custom action — that action does NOT live on the cohort_def viewset. It is on the CONCEPTS viewset (chiron/api/viewsets/concept.py:205 and chiron/api_v2/viewsets/concept.py:219, plus cohort_def_callback_streaming), i.e. out of this scope (concepts resource). agents.notes:
SCOPE COVERED: v2 auth; v1 me, chiron_users, project, version. Base mounting: chiron/urls.py:101 mounts v1 at /api/, chiron/urls.py:102 mounts v2 at /api/v2/. All routes use DRF DefaultRouter with trailing slashes.

ENABLED ACTIONS PER VIEWSET (verified against base classes):
- AuthViewSetV2 (viewsets.ViewSet): only list defined -> only GET /api/v2/auth/. No detail route (no retrieve/etc.).
- MeViewSet (GenericViewSet): only custom list -> only GET /api/me/.
- ChironUserViewSet (ReadOnlyModelViewSet): list + retrieve only. No writes.
- ProjectViewSet (ModelViewSet): list, retrieve, create, update, partial_update, destroy all routed.
- VersionViewSet (GenericViewSet): only custom list -> GET /api/version/.

WHAT THE AUTH ENDPOINT ACTUALLY RETURNS (important): /api/v2/auth/ returns ONLY {user, chironVersion}. It does NOT return permissions, dataset access, or feature flags — despite the task's framing. The auth serializers MODULE (chiron/api_v2/serializers/auth.py) also defines DatasetSerializer / DatasetListSerializers, but those are consumed by DatasetViewSetV2 (chiron/api_v2/viewsets/datasets.py), i.e. the /api/v2/dataset/ endpoints (out of this agent's endpoint scope). That is where the React UI obtains: permissions (accessLevel, accessLevelLabel), dataset access flags (canViewWorkspace, canViewSubjectDetails, selectable, contactEmail), and feature/branding flags (siteTitle, logoUrl, extraHeaderLinks). I modeled DatasetSerializer above so the field-level shape is captured; the datasets ENDPOINTS themselves should be owned by the datasets agent.

Auth response by state: anonymous -> {\"user\": null, \"chironVersion\": \"vX.Y.Z\"}; authenticated -> {\"user\": {id, username, isStaff, name, email}, \"chironVersion\": \"vX.Y.Z\"}.

PAGINATION: chiron is a reusable Django app; DRF settings come from the HOST project. There is no REST_FRAMEWORK config inside the chiron package. The reference test project (test_project/test_settings.py:109-115) sets DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS=PageNumberPagination, PAGE_SIZE=10, DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES=[IsAuthenticated]. Consequences: (a) /api/chiron_users/ list is paginated ({count,next,previous,results}, ?page) ONLY when the host sets a default pagination class — otherwise a bare array. (b) /api/project/ ALWAYS paginated via its explicit LargeResultsSetPagination (page_size 1000, max 10000, ?page & ?page_size). (c) /api/me/, /api/version/, /api/v2/auth/ are custom single-object lists and are never paginated.

VERSION STRING INCONSISTENCY: /api/v2/auth/ returns chironVersion WITH a 'v' prefix; /api/version/ returns chiron WITHOUT the prefix. Both fall back on error ('v0.0.0' vs 'Unknown' respectively).

BUGS/CAVEATS FOUND (in scope):
1. ProjectViewSet.update() calls super().create() (project.py:61) -> PUT /api/project/{id}/ creates a NEW project instead of updating; URL id is ignored; returns 201.
2. ProjectViewSet defines def delete() (project.py:63-70) which is dead code — DRF routes DELETE to destroy (inherited from ModelViewSet), so destroy runs and delete() is never called.
3. ProjectSerializer exposes only {id, name, viewable_report_count}; the required Project.dataset FK is neither in the serializer nor set via a perform_create override, so POST/PUT create would insert dataset=NULL -> IntegrityError. Latent.
4. MeViewSet uses ChironUser.objects.get(user=user) with no dataset filter -> DoesNotExist/MultipleObjectsReturned (HTTP 500) if the user has 0 or >1 ChironUser rows.
5. ChironUserViewSet.get_queryset() does not filter by the active dataset, so list returns ChironUsers across ALL datasets even though DatasetSelector gates access.
open_questions: ChironUserViewSet.get_queryset() (chiron_user.py:18-33) returns ChironUser.objects across ALL datasets with no dataset filter — is cross-dataset exposure intended, or should it be scoped to the request's active dataset like other v1 viewsets?

ProjectViewSet create/update path never sets the required Project.dataset FK (ProjectSerializer omits it, no perform_create override). How does POST /api/project/ actually succeed in practice — is dataset injected somewhere not found (signal, manager default), or is create simply broken/unused by the UI?

ProjectViewSet.update() calling super().create() (project.py:61) appears to be a copy-paste bug making PUT behave as create. Confirm whether the React UI ever issues PUT to /api/project/{id}/ or only POST/PATCH.
The 'active' query param on /api/chiron_users/ uses string logic (value != 'false'); passing active=0 or active=no would evaluate to True (active). Confirm the UI only ever sends 'true'/'false'.

chiron_users pagination shape depends on the host project's DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS. Confirm the production/consumer settings (not just test_settings.py) so the wrapper-vs-bare-array shape is pinned down for the React client.

agents.notes: Scope was DATA MODELS only; endpoints intentionally empty. Read all 6 files in chiron/models/ in full: __init__.py, data_definition_models.py (1360 lines), user_models.py (653), processor_models.py, log_models.py, cache_models.py. 33 concrete Django models returned. TimeStampedModel (defined identically in data_definition_models.py:27, user_models.py:26, processor_models.py:9, cache_models.py:9) is abstract and NOT returned as its own model; its `created` (DateTimeField auto_now_add) and `modified` (DateTimeField auto_now) fields are folded into each concrete subclass that inherits it (AutocreatedField, all *Snapshot, ContentSharing, ContentFlag, Project, UserCreatedContent, CachedConceptStats, CachedCohort). SystemChironUser (user_models.py:37) is a plain Python helper class, NOT a Django model, so excluded. Each model's implicit auto-PK `id` (integer) is included since it appears on the wire. Type mapping used: CharField/SlugField/TextField/EmailField/URLField->string, IntegerField->integer, FloatField->number, BooleanField->boolean, DateTimeField->string(iso8601), ForeignKey->integer(id), ManyToManyField->array<integer(id)>, JSONField->object. IMPORTANT GOTCHAS for a validator: EtlLog.dataset, CachedConceptStats.dataset, and CachedCohort.dataset are SlugFields storing the dataset slug STRING, not ForeignKeys to Dataset (unlike everywhere else where `dataset` is an FK integer id). Several TextFields hold JSON-serialized payloads (CohortDefSnapshot.cohort_def, TableDefSnapshot.table_def, AnalysisDefSnapshot.analysis_def, UserCreatedContent.definition, CachedConceptStats.stats, SourceProcessorArg.value/ConceptHandlerArg.value cast by data_type) - on the wire from the DB these are strings, though API serializers may parse them to objects. `nullable` follows the task's rule (null=True OR blank=True); note Dataset.contact_email is blank-only (no null=True) so DB stores '' not NULL. UserCreatedContent.get_definition() injects a default records_per_page=500 into the parsed definition object. Enum choices captured inline in field notes: AccessLevel(phi/deid/agg), InfobarType(info/warning/danger), Concept.PrefilterMode(required/optional), UserCreatedContent.Type(cohort/table/cohort_auto), ContentFlag.FlagType(star), DataType(string/float/integer/boolean), EtlLog.Status('ETL started'/'ETL completed').
open_questions: Django's AUTH_USER_MODEL (ChironUser.user FK target) is external to chiron/models/ and was not inspected; its field shape (username/first_name/last_name/email etc.) lives in Django's auth app or a custom user model configured in settings.

The abstract TimeStampedModel is defined redundantly in four model files; assumed identical (created=auto_now_add, modified=auto_now). No divergence observed but not cross-diffed field-by-field beyond reading each.

JSON-serialized TextField columns (cohort_def, table_def, analysis_def, definition, stats) have internal object schemas that are not declared at the model layer; their shapes would need to be derived from processors/serializers, out of scope here.

agents.notes:
SCOPE: table_def, analysis_def, analysis_tools (v1 under /api/, v2 under /api/v2/{dataset_string}/). All are plain DRF viewsets.ViewSet (NOT ModelViewSet/GenericViewSet) - so NO pagination wrapper anywhere; responses are hand-built dicts wrapped in Response(). No update/partial_update/destroy actions exist for any of these three resources. NO DRF serializer classes exist for table_def/analysis_def/analysis_tools in chiron/api/serializers.py (that file only has Me/User/ChironUser/ConceptRelated/Category/Concept/Collection/Project/UserCreatedContent serializers); the concept-related ones expose include_in_table_def / include_in_analysis_def boolean flags but are out of scope here.

V2 relationship: TableDefViewSetV2/AnalysisDefViewSetV2/AnalysisToolsViewSetV2 SUBCLASS the v1 viewsets. They only change (a) permission_classes (DatasetSelector -> DatasetUrlPermission, dataset resolved from URL {dataset_string} instead of Django session) and (b) override one method each: table_def/analysis_def override retrieve (v2 scopes the snapshot queryset to request.chironuser via .objects.filter(chironuser=...); v1 does NOT filter, so v1 retrieve can fetch ANY user's snapshot by pk), and analysis_tools overrides list (rewrites hyperlink prefixes to /api/v2/<dataset>/). All other v2 actions (list, create, associated_concept_ids, run_analysis, export_csv) are inherited verbatim.

Routing: DefaultRouter, trailing slashes required. v1 mounted at path('api/', chiron/urls.py:101); v2 at path('api/v2/', chiron/urls.py:102). v2 uses regex prefix r'(?P<dataset_string>.+)/table_def' etc (chiron/api_v2/urls.py:13-23) - dataset_string is a greedy .+ capture.

Auth: all use CsrfExemptSessionAuthentication + IsAuthenticated. Workspace gate via CanViewWorkspacePermission (403 if chironuser.can_view_workspace False). analysis_* also require AnalysisViewOn; table_def requires SubjectLevelAccess.

Transformation type vocab - table_def create: add_entry, bulk_add_entries, duplicate_entry, delete_entry, resort_columns, add_sort_entry, clear_sort_entries, add_category (chiron/api/utils/table_def.py:201). analysis_def create: add_entry, move_entry, delete_entry, clear_all, swap_rows_and_cols (chiron/api/utils/analysis_def.py:126). create endpoints read raw request.body via json.loads (not request.data), require top-level 'transformation' key else HTTP 400.

extended_table_def per-field shape (chiron/query_definition/table_def_functions.py:150-212): entry_id, concept_id, concept_name, collection{collection_id,event_date_field(nullable),event_end_date_field(nullable)}, categories[str], label, can_delete(bool), can_sort(bool), has_errors(bool), aggregate(bool), alias(nullable), categorize(bool); if aggregate: +aggregation_method, aggregation_settings, aggregation_criteria_set, aggregation_criteria_set_name. Missing-concept fields get a reduced dict (entry_id, concept_id, categories:[], label=concept_id, has_errors:True, can_delete:True, can_sort:True, aggregate).

run_analysis dataset field = json.loads(pandas df.to_json(orient='split')) => {columns:[...], index:[...], data:[[...]]}, or null when analysis_def has neither rows nor cols. Content negotiation: JSON default, text/plain renders pivottable.html / analysis_metadata.html templates, text/html BrowsableAPI.
open_questions: AnalysisToolsViewSet.list emits the 'run_analysis' hyperlink as <list-url>+'preview_metadata' (both v1 analysis_tools.py:41 and v2 analysis_tools.py:24), but the actual @action route is named 'run_analysis' (DRF url_path defaults to the method name). No 'preview_metadata' action is defined in these viewsets, so the advertised URL appears to 404. Likely a stale/renamed-action bug - confirm whether a preview_metadata route exists elsewhere or the UI ignores this field.

AnalysisToolsViewSet._get_analysis_def (analysis_tools.py:140-149) checks `if 'table_def' in request.GET` but then reads request.GET['analysis_def']. This means the GET branch only fires when a 'table_def' param is present, and a raw 'analysis_def' GET param without 'table_def' would fall through to the active analysis_def. Looks like a copy-paste bug from the table_def viewset - confirm intended query param name for run_analysis/export_csv GET.

export_csv docstring documents a 'table_def' param but the code path uses analysis_def (self._get_analysis_def). Confirm whether table_def is actually consumed anywhere for CSV export or is purely vestigial doc.

The task referenced 'TableDefinition / AnalysisDefinition' models, but no such model classes exist - the real persisted models are TableDefSnapshot / AnalysisDefSnapshot (user_models.py), and the table_def/analysis_def payloads are untyped JSON TextFields. Field types inside those JSON blobs are inferred from usage in query_definition/*.py and api/utils/*.py, not from a schema/serializer.

get_active_table_def/get_active_analysis_def return default {'fields': []} when no active snapshot, but analysis_def consumers expect {rows, cols}; the {'fields':[]} default for analysis_def (user_models.py:450) is shape-inconsistent with the rest of the analysis pipeline - confirm whether this default is ever hit in practice.
